full_judgment:
2. The facts, as stated in this petition, in short, are that respondent No. 8, the Thana Nirbahi Officer of Hajiganj, Chandpur by his Memo No. 9-5/96-308/dated 24-6-1996 referring Memo No. PROJE-3/Misc.-37/941 307(64) dated 16-5-1996 issued by respondent No. 3, the Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives, Local Government Division, instructed Proforma respondent No. 10, the then Chairman, No.1 Rajargaon (Uttar) Union Parishad to divide existing three wards of his Union Parishad into 9 Wards and send a list of village-based wards to him by 30-6-1996. Proforma respondent No. 10 called for a meeting in the Union Parishad Office on 8-7-1996 and in presence of eight elected Union Parishad members divided the three existing wards into nine wards upon thorough and detailed discussion and considering territorial unity, distribution of population and administrative convenience in accordance with the prescribed form sent to him by respondent No. 8 and forwarded the same together with minutes of the meeting, List of newly constituted 9 wards showing number of voters, names of the villages and a sketch map showing their geographical location, vide Annexure-C, C-1, and C-2 to respondent No. 8 on 10-7-1996. 

 3. Respondent No. 8 thereafter referred the matter to respondent No. 9, the delimitation officer and respondent No. 9 informed proforma respondent No. 10 that a meeting would be held on 24-8-1996 in the Union Parishad office to finalise the delimitation/reconstitution of wards and hear objections, if any, and under his instructions proforma respondent No. 10 made publicity by miking to make sure of the presence of the local people and Union Parishad members. 

 4. In Annexure-C-1, i.e, List of newly constituted 9 wards the village named Pipya was included in ward No. 4 along with villages named Menapur and Niraine. 

 5. One Lokman Patwari, former Chairman of the said Union Parisad, took an objection to respondent No. 9 on 4-9-1996 about inclusion of the village Pipya with ward No. 4 and respondent No. 9 by Annexure-E notified Lokman Patwari that a discussion meeting would be held on 9-9-1996 in the said Union Parisad office about inclusion of the Pipya village with newly constituted wards and that he will physically visit the Pipya village after the said meeting requesting him to attend the meeting with documents and witnesses in his support also instructing proforma respondent No. 10 to prepare a list of male female inhabitants and number of voters in each village and also ensure attendance of the members of the Union Parisad in the meeting. 

 7. It is alleged that the said Lokman Patwari did neither appear before the delimitation officer nor substantiate his objection. He rather approached the Thana Nirbahi Officer, respondent No. 8, who most illegally excluded the Pipya village from ward No. 4 and included it with ward No. 6 and sent the list of 9 newly constituted wards of respondent No. 2 for publication in the Bangladesh Gazette. In the Bangladesh Gazette published on 12-10-1996 (Annexure-G) the Pipya village was included with the ward No. 6 behind the back of the petitioner and people of the Pipya village. The petitioner is an intending candidate for the post of Union Parisad member from this Pipya village. For the first time on 11-10-2002 the petitioner came to learn about the Gazette notification and inclusion of Pipya village with ward No. 6 instead of ward No. 4. He then made representations in writing to respondent No. 8 and respondent No. 5, the District Election Officer, chandpur on 13-10-2000, vide Annexure-I and J stating that the villages of ward No. 6 are far away from the Pipya village and that the communication system is not good. On the other hand, other two villages in ward No. 4 situate next to the Pipya village, communication is good, all the villagers are living in the same society. 

 9. Mr NH Khandakar, Learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that division of existing three wards into 9 wards is legal, valid and lawful but inclusion of the Pipya village with ward No. 6 instead of ward No. 4 is illegal, arbitrary and malafide. The voters of the Pipya village will have to go to the vote centre in ward No. 6 by crossing through the chowk and during the rainy season the chowk goes under water. The Pipya villagers are closer from all respects to Menapur village under ward No. 4. Inclusion of the Pipya village with ward No. 6 was done in violation of section 20 of the Local Government (Union Parisad) Ordinance, 1983. 

 11. Section 19 of the Local Government (Union Parisad) Ordinance, 1983 provides for appointment of delimitation officer by the Thana Nirbahi Officer from amongst persons in service of the Republic. The delimitation officer shall follow the procedure laid down in section 20 of the Ordinance in delimiting the wards. Section 20 of the Local Government (Union Parisad) Ordinance, 1983 is quoted below. 

 "20. Delimitation wards-(1) The wards shall be delimited having regard to territorial unity and, so far as practicable, to distribution of population and administrative convenience. 

 (2) A delimitation officer may, for the purpose of delimiting the wards, make such enquiries and examine such records as he may deem necessary and consider such representations as may be received by him, and shall publish at his office and at the office of the Union parisad and at such other place or places as he considers necessary a preliminary list of wards specifying the areas proposed to be included in each such ward together with a notice inviting objections or suggestions within fifteen days from the date of publication of the notice. 

 (5) After making amendments, alteration of modifications, if any, under sub-section (4), the delimitation officer shall publish at his office and at the office of the Union Parisad and at such other place or places as he considers necessary the final list of wards, specifying the areas included in such ward and shall forward attested copies thereof to the Thana Nirbahi Officer, who shall publish the list of wards in the official Gazette." 

 12. It appears from Annexure-C-2 that the Pipya village is adjacent to Menapur village under ward No. 4 and the people of Pipya village have exercised their right of franchise in the Menapur polling centre for long as per finding of respondent No. 9 vide Annexure-F. During the division of the three wards into 9 wards this Pipya village was placed under ward No. 4 along with Menapur and Niraine villages by the Chairman and members of the Union Parisad. A former Chairman, who is an inhabitant of Ward No. 5, raised an objection to inclusion of the Pipya village with Menapur under ward No. 4 and, according to him, it should be included with ward No. 6 The delimitation officer made an enquiry into the matter on 9-9-1996 and in local inspection found that the people of the Pipya village would cast their votes in Menapur village centre from before. Mouza Number of Pipya and Menapur villages is one and same, i-e, 179. There is no good communication between Rajargaon, i.e ward No. 6, and the Pipya village, socially they are co-related with Menapur village and that from the point of distribution of population i-e, voter-consistency, it is convenient for them to remain with the Menapur village and no one from the Pipya village ever raised any objection to inclusion of the village to ward No. 4. 

 13. Under sub-section (3) of section 20 of the Ordinance the Thana Nirbahi Officer may make an inquiry if he receives any objection or suggestion about delimitation and shall give his decision within 15 days and send it to the delimitation officer and under sub-section (4) the delimitation officer shall make such amendments, alterations or modifications in the preliminary list as may be required by any such decision. Thereafter the delimitation officer shall publish final list at specified places and shall send attested copies thereof to the Thana Nirbahi Officer who shall publish the list of wards in the official Gazette in accordance with sub-section (5). But in the instant case, the Thana Nirbahi Officer, respondent No. 8, in violation of procedure laid down in section 20 included the Pipya village with ward No. 6 behind the back of the villagers and without making any inquiry or suggestion whatsoever and before publication of final list according to the procedure, sent the same to respondent No. 2 for publication in the Bangladesh Gazette and the impugned Gazette notification was thus published. 

 14. Under section 20 of the Local Government (Union Parisad) Ordinance, 1983 only the delimitation officer is responsible for making preliminary and final list of wards. After publishing preliminary list he can make amendment, alteration, modification, if any. The Thana Nirbahi Officer may give his decision on specific matter to the delimitation officer owing to which the delimitation officer may make an amendment, alteration or modification or necessary correction of any error or omission in the preliminary list and shall thereafter publish the final list in the manner prescribed in sub-section (5) and only after that the Thana Nirbahi Officer shall publish the final list in the official Gazette. 

 15. In the instant case there is nothing to show that the Thana Nirbani Officer ever made any inquiry, decision or suggestion to the delimitation officer and the delimitation officer ever made any amendment, alteration modification in the preliminary list. It appears that bypassing the delimitation officer and denying sentiment of the inhabitants of the Pipya village, ignoring their communication and other social and practical inconveniences and territorial unity the Thana Nirbahi Officer, respondent No. 8 sent the list of 9 wards to respondent No. 2 for publication in the Bangladesh Gazette including the Pipya village in ward No. 6 to utter disappointment of the inhabitants of that village and paving ways for litigation's resulting in impasse in the elections of that Union Parisad. No election was held in his Union Parisad, according to the Learned Assistant Attorney General, after 1992. The Thana Nirbahi Officer has acted beyond his jurisdiction and pangs have drawn the people up to this court. 

 18. It further appears that the Election Commission by Memo No. NIKS/Stha" Ni-I/E" PA/2(56)96/751 dated 9-10-2000 instructed respondent No. 5, the District Election Officer, Chandpur to hold General Election in this Union in view of disposal of Writ Petition No. 6772 of 1992, vide Annexure-H. Though there was no order of stay of election from this Court in this Writ Petition but still the District Election Officer did not arrange for holding election in accordance with Annexure-H for reasons best known to him.
